## Body

**Performance: pass-with-notes** at `1d9a1f30fbee5b3bce5b09a8bb084947a9dba997`.

**F114's new pane probe launches nothing.** The new path is reached only for a refreshed, non-tombstoned descriptor with `proc == None`; no recorded pane means no probe. `list_panes_without_launch` uses `control.query_live`, whose `may_start = false` prevents client creation. Unavailable/failed control returns unknown, never the ordinary forking `list_panes` fallback. The default port implementation also refuses observation rather than launching. Bound/healthy seats keep the prior path.

**P174-N001: the cost is not strictly one query per such seat per tick.** The reaper checks eligibility once, then checks it again before a non-dry-run tombstone. Define B as current never-bound, pane-recorded seats and C as those whose first observation is eligible. The added strict-probe budget is **B+C calls per existing default 5-second sweep**, at most **2B**; actual control requests require a live client. Retained/unknown seats get one check; eligible seats get two even if the final CAS conflicts. Four consistently absent leftovers therefore take up to **eight**, not four, pane-list reads on their retirement sweep.

Every successful read returns/parses the session/server pane list and scans it for the recorded ID. With F returned panes, this is O((B+C)*F) parsing/search work, with no shared per-sweep pane snapshot. Path and output bytes also matter. The existing synchronous control read can wait up to its 3-second reply timeout; it adds no fork but can occupy the caller and delay the serialized tick. The existing scheduler does not overlap or burst-catch-up slow sweeps.

The predicate limits the work to never-bound seats, **not to a hard cardinality of four**. There is no new cap, expiry or probe backoff. A present pane with no registration can keep taking this path indefinitely; a healthy registration window is brief by observation, not an enforced deadline. The four retire only when both observations and the CAS succeed. Additional steady-state probe work is zero when B=0, not a guarantee while the control client is unavailable or new pre-bind seats remain. Existing registry list/get work and bound-seat probes continue.

Retirement keeps the existing tombstone/notice machinery. The strict eligibility probe is process-free; a notice to a surviving parent still uses existing delivery and its possible launches. Queued jobs are retained, not deleted. No new executable site, loop or timer is added; the six spawn guards are unchanged and pass.

**F115's added write:** only an admitted dormant digest with listed holds calls the existing `flag_shown` helper. It uses the IDs already in the view: one schema check, one owned transaction and **H UPSERT statements** for H listed job IDs, plus O(H) ID copying. It is not one constant-size SQL statement. Empty/refused/failed-admission digests skip it; store errors are logged. The existing dormant claim gates attempts per quiet stretch (default 30 minutes), so this is not a write every PA tick. “Shown” means the digest was admitted as delivered/queued/held, not that the PA/model read it. Other digest paths already use this helper.
